universe: Top 432 NSE stocks by traded value

strategies.name: 44-DMA cross-up
strategies.rule: Close crosses above the 44-day average and finishes within 5% of it.
strategies.exit: Sell at the target (+20%), the stop loss (-8%), or after 40 trading days, whichever comes first.

strategies.name: 44-DMA buy zone (rising)
strategies.rule: First day the close is 0 to 5% above a rising 44-day average (the average is higher than 5 days ago).
strategies.exit: Sell at the target (+20%), the stop loss (-8%), or after 40 trading days, whichever comes first.

strategies.name: 44-DMA pullback
strategies.rule: Rising 44-day average; the stock was at least 8% above it in the last 20 days, then falls back to within 2% above it.
strategies.exit: Sell at the target (+20%), the stop loss (-8%), or after 40 trading days, whichever comes first.

strategies.name: 20/50 average cross
strategies.rule: The 20-day average crosses above the 50-day average.
strategies.exit: Sell at the target (+20%), the stop loss (-8%), or after 40 trading days, whichever comes first.

strategies.name: Pullback to the 50-DMA in an uptrend
strategies.rule: 50-day average above the 200-day; the close comes back up through the 50-day average and finishes within 3% of it.
strategies.exit: Sell at the target (+20%), the stop loss (-8%), or after 40 trading days, whichever comes first.

strategies.name: 52-week high breakout
strategies.rule: Close above the highest close of the last 252 days, with volume above 1.5 times the 20-day average.
strategies.exit: Sell at the target (+20%), the stop loss (-8%), or after 40 trading days, whichever comes first.

strategies.name: Base breakout
strategies.rule: Close above the highest close of the last 40 days, after a base no wider than 25% from low to high.
strategies.exit: Sell at the target (+20%), the stop loss (-8%), or after 40 trading days, whichever comes first.

strategies.name: 20-day high breakout
strategies.rule: Close above the highest high of the last 20 days while above the 100-day average.
strategies.exit: Sell at the target (+20%), the stop loss (-8%), or after 40 trading days, whichever comes first.

strategies.name: Strong momentum
strategies.rule: Up more than 20% in 6 months, within 10% of its 52-week high and above its 50-day average (first day only).
strategies.exit: Sell at the target (+20%), the stop loss (-8%), or after 40 trading days, whichever comes first.

strategies.name: Volatility squeeze breakout
strategies.rule: After the Bollinger bands were at their tightest 10% of the last 120 days (within 5 days), the close breaks above the upper band, above the 50-day average.
strategies.exit: Sell at the target (+20%), the stop loss (-8%), or after 40 trading days, whichever comes first.

strategies.name: Narrow-range breakout (NR7)
strategies.rule: Yesterday had the narrowest day range of the last 7; today closes above yesterday's high, above the 50-day average.
strategies.exit: Sell at the target (+20%), the stop loss (-8%), or after 40 trading days, whichever comes first.

strategies.name: Gap-up on volume
strategies.rule: Opens more than 2% above yesterday's high, closes above its open, volume at least 2 times average, above the 50-day average.
strategies.exit: Sell at the target (+20%), the stop loss (-8%), or after 40 trading days, whichever comes first.

strategies.name: Volume surge
strategies.rule: Volume at least 2 times the 20-day average and up 3% or more on the day, while above the 50-day average.
strategies.exit: Sell at the target (+20%), the stop loss (-8%), or after 40 trading days, whichever comes first.

strategies.name: Supertrend flip up
strategies.rule: The Supertrend (10 days, 3 times ATR) turns up, with the close above the 100-day average.
strategies.exit: Sell at the target (+20%), the stop loss (-8%), or after 40 trading days, whichever comes first.

strategies.name: MACD cross in an uptrend
strategies.rule: MACD crosses above its signal line while still below zero, with the close above the 200-day average.
strategies.exit: Sell at the target (+20%), the stop loss (-8%), or after 40 trading days, whichever comes first.

strategies.name: Oversold in an uptrend (RSI 14)
strategies.rule: Close above the 200-day average while the 14-day RSI is below 35.
strategies.exit: Sell at the target (+12%), the stop loss (-6%), or after 15 trading days, whichever comes first.

strategies.name: Extreme dip (RSI 2)
strategies.rule: Close above the 200-day average while the 2-day RSI is below 10.
strategies.exit: Sell at the target (+12%), the stop loss (-6%), or after 15 trading days, whichever comes first.

strategies.name: Dip below the lower Bollinger band
strategies.rule: First close below the lower Bollinger band (20 days, 2 deviations) while above the 200-day average.
strategies.exit: Sell at the target (+12%), the stop loss (-6%), or after 15 trading days, whichever comes first.

strategies.name: Bounce after a 5% slide
strategies.rule: Above the 200-day average, down more than 5% over 5 days, then an up day that closes above yesterday's high.
strategies.exit: Sell at the target (+12%), the stop loss (-6%), or after 15 trading days, whichever comes first.

caveats: A signal is bought at the next day's open; every trade pays 0.4% round-trip costs; the stop is assumed to hit first if a day touches both stop and target.
The stop and target for each strategy were chosen on the earlier 60% of the history and judged on the later 40% only.
Past results do not predict the future. Testing many strategies means some will look good by luck: trust the ones with many trades, a clear edge and profits in most years.
The stock list is today's liquid stocks, so stocks that were delisted are missing and results look better than real life would have been.
News, results announcements and company events are not part of the test.
